_comment: Prose claims that something DOES NOT EXIST in the corpus. `absence_audit.py` re-runs each registered search and fails if it now matches. Registering an absence claim WITHOUT a search that could falsify it is the anti-pattern this registry exists to discourage -- a claim nothing can refute is not checked, it is merely written down.
_provenance: Seeded 2026-08-28 after three claims in CLAUDE.md were found false: mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left (exists), min and abs (both exist in Basic.lean and are used). Every entry below was re-verified against the corpus at registration; the ones that failed were fixed rather than registered.

claim_text: These order lemmas do NOT exist here

claims.note: mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left was on this list and DOES exist; removed from the prose and from this pattern.

Upgraded 2026-08-28 from a grep for `^syntax "linarith"` to a compile probe. The grep proved nobody DECLARED it here; only compiling proves it is unavailable, which is what the gotcha actually claims.

claim_text: measure theory, which does not exist anywhere in MachLib
claims.note: Narrowed at registration: the prose said 'measure AND integration theory', but a monotone Riemann integral (RiemannIntegralMonotone) and several Gaussian integrals DO exist, added the same day. Measure theory is the part that is genuinely absent, and is what the search checks.

claim_text: because there is no `#eval` path at all
claims.note: SAFETY-RELEVANT, and the best kind of absence claim to register: it is the reason a numerical spot-check cannot inhabit `Meets` and be mistaken for a discharged obligation. If an #eval ever lands in MachLib/, that argument needs re-reading before the claim is re-worded. 0 occurrences at registration.

claim_text: there is no other way to write a constant at this layer
claims.note: MachLib.Real carries OfNat for 0 and 1 only (Basic.lean:38-39). This is why numerals must be written as natCast N, which is the single most repeated tactic gotcha in the corpus. Verified: exactly 2 OfNat Real instances at registration. NOTE ON THE PATTERN: it first used a negative lookahead `(?!Zero|One)`, which grep -E does not support (POSIX ERE has none), so it matched instOfNatOne and reported a false NOW-FALSE. That failure was LOUD. The dangerous direction is the opposite one -- a search too NARROW to match anything passes silently, and nothing in this auditor detects it.
